chart-data.area: Trading PWA price chart data pipeline (NewChart.jsx ← lineChartStore ← useWebSocket ← API /line-chart + main ws gateway ← redis.subscriber ← engine price.tick)
chart-data.architecture: Engine: every executed trade (real or NPC) goes through trade-executed.handler.ts → MarketStateService.applyTradeExecuted (price from imbalance; `volumeScale = resolveTradeVolumeNotional(payload)` = trade $ amount) → BattleEventsPublisher.priceTick publishes `engine:events:price.tick` {battleId, price, displayPrice, timestamp: Date.now() ms, volumeScale}, but only if `shouldPublishEnginePriceTick` (200 ms per-battle coalescer) allows it; skipped ticks are dropped outright. The engine also runs its own CandleProjectionService (Redis `active:candle:<id>:1000`, DB `candles`, CANDLE_CLOSED/ACTIVE channels) which nothing in the API consumes. API (apps/api/src/redis/redis.subscriber.ts): the broadcaster-leader worker receives price.tick, dedupes by `price:${battle}:${ms}:${price}:${source}`, feeds LineChartGateway.handlePriceTick (aggregates 1-second OHLC + summed `volumeScale` into in-memory `liveCandles` for keys `battle_<id>` and `all`, persists closed candles to Redis zsets `chart:history:battle_<id>` (trimmed to MAX_POINTS=200) and list `ticktrade:candle:history`), and separately coalesces `priceUpdate` (200 ms) to the main socket room `battle_<id>` with `timestamp: floor(ms/1000)` seconds and `price = displayPrice`. A 1 Hz boundary timer closes candles (flat candles when idle) and publishes `candleClosed` (timestamp = bucket start in seconds, battle_id) over Redis `chart:events:closed` → every API worker forwards to its `/line-chart` room (`line_chart_all` for the client's default scope 'all'). On subscribe/connect and on each `battle.started`, `buildCandleBatchPayload` emits `candleBatch` containing ONLY the last 3 COMPLETED battles (archive zset `chart:history:completed:<id>`, else DB rebuild from `price_ticks` with volume = tick count), deduped by timestamp and sliced to 200 total points; the active battle's closed candles are never sent. Client (utils/useWebSocket.js): main socket `priceUpdate` → 40 ms throttle → RAF flush → lineChartStore.upsertLatestCandle (tick candle for the current second, volume 0); `/line-chart` `candleBatch` → appendCandleBatch + markServerHistoryReady; `candleClosed` → appendCandleBatch (dedupe key `ms:battle_id`, so the closed candle replaces the tick candle) + sessionStorage `tt_linechart_candleClosed_session_v1`; battle transitions call resetLineChart + unsubscribe/resubscribe (60–100 ms gap). NewChart.jsx merges store prices with the per-tab sessionStorage candles (`mergePricesWithSessionClosed`), slices to 200 points, builds an AreaSeries (close) + overlay HistogramSeries (server `volume`), does setData on first load / regressions and series.update for appends, and a RAF loop eases the last bar's value toward the latest tick (`series.update({time: lastTimeRef, value: display})`). Timestamps are UTC epoch seconds end to end; no local-time bucketing; the client never derives OHLC/volume itself; the PWA service worker (vite.config.js) caches only static assets (NetworkOnly for navigations; no API/socket caching).

findings.title: candleBatch never includes the ACTIVE battle; clients bootstrap with hours-old completed battles and then jump to the live price
findings.user_symptom: (1) sudden spike line right after signing in / reconnecting on the phone; (2) charts differ per device
findings.evidence: line-chart.gateway.ts:639-648 `getLastCompletedBattleIds(): … where: { status: 'COMPLETED' }, orderBy: { id: 'desc' }, take: HISTORY_BATTLE_LIMIT` and :820-836 `buildCandleBatchPayload … for (const bid of includedBattleIds) { const candles = await this.getClosedCandlesForBattle(bid, now) …}` — `activeBattleId` is looked up (:823-828) but only echoed as `active_battle_id`, never used to fetch candles. The active battle's closed candles DO exist: observed `chart:history:battle_80 ZCARD=192` while battle 80 was ACTIVE. Live DB at audit time: battle 80 ACTIVE started 13:52:28 UTC at ~1.2388; the three COMPLETED battles served (77,78,79) ended 01:07–01:18 UTC at 1.286–1.296. Client side: useWebSocket.js:565-583 `onCandleBatch … appendCandleBatch(normalizedCandles)`; NewChart.jsx:1498 effect deps `[api, activeBattleId, serverHistoryReady, chartEngineReady]` re-run on serverHistoryReady → applyFullSeriesReset sets `displayValueRef.current = last.value` (:1273, the 12-hour-old close) → first `priceUpdate` sets pendingTarget to the live price and the RAF (:1077 `areaSeriesRef.current.update({ time: lastTimeRef.current, value: display })`) eases from the stale close to the live price; the area series then draws a single steep segment between the last stale candle and the first live bar (lightweight-charts renders consecutive points adjacently — no time gap).
findings.mechanism: On connect/reconnect the only history the client can get is completed battles (hours old, different price regime). The current round's already-closed seconds are never sent, so the series goes old-close → live-price in one bar: visually a vertical spike/drop, animated by the easing loop. The same happens after a phone backgrounds and the socket reconnects: live candles missed while backgrounded are not backfilled. Also `applyDefaultChartZoom` (NewChart.jsx:236-255) fits the price scale to the last 80 bars, which span both regimes, exaggerating the jump.
findings.fix_sketch: line-chart.gateway.ts buildCandleBatchPayload: include the active battle's closed candles (in-memory `historyByKey.get('battle_<active>')` / Redis `chart:history:battle_<active>`) and cap by a time window (e.g. last N seconds) rather than 'last 3 COMPLETED ids'; optionally also emit the in-progress candle from `liveCandles`. Client: on candleBatch always setData the server window and drop any local candles older than the batch's first timestamp; on reconnect request a backfill `since=lastTimeRef`.

findings.evidence: NewChart.jsx:143-163 `mergePricesWithSessionClosed` merges `loadCandleClosedSessionForBattle(bid)` (sessionStorage `tt_linechart_candleClosed_session_v1`, persistCandleClosedSession.js:31-62) into the series; :1301 `candles = mergePricesWithSessionClosed(candles, activeBattleId)`; :29 `MAX_SERIES_POINTS = STABILITY.MAX_CHART_POINTS` (=200, core/constants.js:13) vs store cap `MAX_CANDLES: 300` (constants.js:12, lineChartStore.js:5). ResumeSyncBridge.jsx:119/145/191/206 saves `recentCandles: prices.slice(-50)` (tick candles included) and hydrateMatchFromResume.js:88-97 seeds `lineChartStore.hydrateFromSessionClosedCandles(candles)` on reload. useWebSocket.js:1002 `if (now - priceTickLastForwardedAtRef.current < 40) { droppedPriceTickCountRef… return; }` (per-device tick drop). Combined with F1 (active-battle history only from connect time onward).
findings.mechanism: Each client's series = candleBatch(3 completed battles, ≤200 pts) ∪ candleClosed received since its own connect ∪ its own tick candles ∪ its own tab's sessionStorage/resume candles, then trimmed to the last 200/300 entries. Two devices connecting at different times, or one tab refreshed vs a fresh device, hold different sets, so the x-range, the first visible bar and the price-scale fit differ.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the server the single source: serve a canonical window (active battle full closed history + previous battle tail, fixed count/time span) on every connect/resubscribe and on a `since` backfill; on candleBatch replace (not merge) client history; remove the sessionStorage/resume candle merges (or only use them until the first candleBatch and then discard); align MAX_CANDLES/MAX_SERIES_POINTS with the server window.

findings.title: Engine 200 ms tick coalescer drops trades' volume (volumeScale) instead of accumulating it; API ms-level dedupe drops more
findings.user_symptom: (3) $100k order raised the bar, a ~$10k order later produced the same/higher bar
findings.evidence: price-tick-coalesce.ts:12-19 `shouldPublishEnginePriceTick(battleId) { … if (now - last < PRICE_TICK_COALESCE_MS) return false; …}` (200 ms). trade-executed.handler.ts:276 `const publishPriceTick = shouldPublishEnginePriceTick(v1.battleId);` :281-300 `if (publishPriceTick) { … await this.events.priceTick(v1.battleId, state.lastPrice, displayPrice, volumeScale, {...}) }` — when false, nothing is published and `volumeScale` (= trade $ amount, market-state.service.ts:196 `resolveTradeVolumeNotional(payload)` / :236 `volumeScale: tradeVolumeNotional`) is discarded. API side sums only what arrives: line-chart.gateway.ts:936 `const tickVolume = Math.max(0, payload.volumeScale ?? 0)`, candle-aggregation.ts:57 `state.volume += Math.max(0, volume)`. Additional drop: redis.subscriber.ts:815-818 `dedupeKey = price:${battleId}:${eventTime}:${price}:${source}; if (this.priceTickDedupeKeys.has(dedupeKey)) return;` (two trades in the same ms at the same rounded price → second one's volume lost). Comment at redis.subscriber.ts:205 says engine publishes ~50 snapshots/sec at NPC peak, i.e. ≥90% of ticks are coalesced under load. Observed check in this quiet env (battle 80, 200-bar window): API zset sum 67,520 == engine per-trade `candles` sum 67,520 — no loss when trades are >200 ms apart, so the loss only manifests under bursty/NPC load.
findings.mechanism: Volume per candle is the sum of `volumeScale` of PUBLISHED ticks. A real $100k order that lands within 200 ms of a preceding tick (very likely during NPC bursts) is never published, so its notional never reaches the candle; a later $10k order that happens to be the first tick in its window is counted. Bars therefore reflect sampling luck, not traded notional.
findings.fix_sketch: In trade-executed.handler.ts keep a per-battle `pendingVolume` accumulator: add `volumeScale` when the coalescer returns false and flush the accumulated sum on the next published tick (or publish a tick when a real-user trade occurs regardless of the coalescer). Alternative: aggregate candle volume in the API from `trade.priced.v1` (TRADE_PRICED_CHANNEL, never coalesced, already carries `amount`) instead of `price.tick.volumeScale`. Make the API dedupe key include eventId, not (ms, price).

findings.title: Volume units are mixed in one histogram: DB-rebuilt history uses tick COUNT, live/archived candles use $ notional; NPC and real notional are summed with no attribution
findings.user_symptom: (3) volume bars look inconsistent/wrong
findings.evidence: line-chart.gateway.ts:669-678 `// Historical rebuild path … fall back to tick-count volume here (volume += 1 per tick)` → `createCandleState(bucketStartMs, price, 1)` / `applyTickToState(carryOver, price, 1)`; used by :731-733 `if (normalized.length === 0) normalized = await this.getClosedCandlesForBattleFromDb(...)`. Observed: no `chart:history:completed:*` keys existed for battles 77–79 (Redis scan) while `price_ticks` had 85/70/90 rows for them → served with volume 1–3 per bar; after battle 80 ended `chart:history:completed:80` appeared with $ volume (sum 67,520), so a client connecting now gets bars of ~1 next to bars of 50–10,000+. Mixing: market-state.service.ts:175 `isNpcOrder = payload.userId === 0` only affects attribution; :196/:236 volumeScale is the notional for both; UnifiedCandlePayload (candle-types.ts:41-52) has no real/npc split.
findings.mechanism: The overlay histogram autoscale (NewChart.jsx:910 `priceScaleId: ""`, :916 scaleMargins) is dominated by whichever unit is larger in the visible window, so history bars flatten to nothing and a single $ bar looks like the only volume; NPC fills (the majority of $ volume) inflate bars unrelated to the user's own orders.
findings.fix_sketch: Persist real notional in the DB path (join `price_ticks.tradeAmount`, column exists: `price_ticks(id, battleId, price, createdAt, deltaPips, tradeAmount, tradeSide, source)`) or read the engine `candles` table (already per-trade notional) instead of tick count; add `real_volume`/`npc_volume` (or `count`) to UnifiedCandlePayload and let the client choose; consider a log/fixed-max volume scale.

findings.title: MAX_POINTS=200 truncates every 300 s battle to its last 200 s and the whole candleBatch to 200 points (effectively only the last completed battle)
findings.user_symptom: (2) history differs from what a long-connected device has; first 100 s of each round vanish from history
findings.evidence: candle-types.ts:7 `MAX_POINTS = 200`; line-chart.gateway.ts:505-508 `zadd … then zremrangebyrank(redisKey, 0, -(MAX_POINTS + 1))` on every close; :794-797 archive trim; :897-898 `if (deduped.length <= MAX_POINTS) return deduped; return deduped.slice(-MAX_POINTS);`. Observed: `chart:history:completed:80` first candle 13:54:08 while battle 80 started 13:52:28 (first 100 s gone); DB battles have `durationSeconds=300`. Payload still advertises `included_battle_ids: [3 ids]` (:857).
findings.mechanism: A device that watched the whole round keeps up to 300 candles (client cap) including the first 100 s; a device that connects later gets ≤200 candles total across '3' battles — different data sets, and the round-entry region (ROUND ENTRY line) has no candles.
findings.fix_sketch: Raise MAX_POINTS to ≥ battle duration (or key the window by time), cap the batch per battle rather than globally, and align client MAX_CANDLES/MAX_CHART_POINTS with it.

findings.title: RAF easing writes interpolated values into series bars; closed bars keep the last eased sample, not the server close (frame-rate/background dependent)
findings.user_symptom: (2) same data renders differently across devices; small residual wiggles
findings.evidence: NewChart.jsx:1077 `areaSeriesRef.current.update({ time: lastTimeRef.current, value: display });` runs every frame with `display += (target - display) * alphaDisplay` (DISPLAY_TAU_MS=88, dt clamped by MAX_FRAME_DELTA_MS=80). candleClosed handling (:1404-1470) only sets `pendingTargetRef.current = closePrice` (:1435/:1444/:1466) and advances `lastTimeRef`; the store path writes the server value once (:1344 `areaSeriesRef.current.update(p)`) but the RAF immediately overwrites the same bar with `display`. When the next bar starts, the previous bar is frozen at whatever `display` had reached. In background tabs/phones RAF is paused, so the last bar freezes at an unconverged value until a full setData.
findings.mechanism: Rendered bar values are animation samples that depend on frame timing and tick arrival timing on each device rather than server candle closes, so two devices with identical server data can still differ pixel-wise, and a device resumed from background shows a wrong last bar.
findings.fix_sketch: On candleClosed (and when advancing lastTimeRef) write `series.update({ time: closedTime, value: close })` for the closed bar before moving on; ease only the in-progress bar; on visibilitychange→visible re-setData from the store; optionally drop easing on mobile.

findings.title: In-progress bar has volume 0 until candleClosed; overlay histogram autoscale rescales when large bars scroll out of the 80-bar view
findings.user_symptom: (3) a later small order 'looks' as tall as an earlier $100k one
findings.evidence: priceUpdate payload (redis.subscriber.ts:878-886) has no volume field; chartNormalization.js:17 `volume: payload.volume ?? 0`; lineChartStore.js:147-150 keeps `prevVol` only if incoming is 0 — so the live bar is 0 until the server's candleClosed one second later. NewChart.jsx:910 `priceScaleId: ""` overlay with default autoscale; applyDefaultChartZoom (:236-255) only pins the right price scale (`ps.setAutoScale(false)`), the volume overlay keeps autoscaling to the visible range; INITIAL_VISIBLE_BARS=80 (:28).
findings.mechanism: With autoscale relative to visible bars, once the $100k bar scrolls out of the ~80-bar window (≈80 s), a $10k bar becomes the visible max and renders at full height; the order's own second also shows no bar for up to 1 s. Combined with F3 (the $100k may not even be counted) this matches the reported observation.
findings.fix_sketch: Include `volume` of the live bucket in priceUpdate (gateway has `existing.volume`) or emit a lightweight `candleUpdate`; anchor the histogram scale (fixed max per round or log scale) so bar height is comparable across time.

findings.title: Resubscribe leaves the line-chart room for 60–100 ms on every battle switch/reconnect; missed candleClosed is never backfilled
findings.user_symptom: (2) occasional missing second per device
findings.evidence: useWebSocket.js:273-283 `resubscribeLineChart … lineChartSocket.emit("unsubscribe", { scope: "all" }); setTimeout(doSubscribe, delayMs);` (default 60; battleSnapshotTransitionService/newBattleStarted pass 80; reconnectPolicyService.js:24 passes 100). line-chart.gateway.ts:579-581 `if (scope === 'all') { socket.leave(ALL_ROOM); return; }` — a boundary `candleClosed` emitted in that window is lost and, per F1, not in candleBatch. Also handleConnection (:255-263) plus the client's own `subscribe` on connect (:524-530) emit two candleBatch payloads per connect (harmless dedupe).
findings.mechanism: Room membership gap at each transition; different devices lose different seconds.
findings.fix_sketch: Don't unsubscribe before subscribe (server subscribe is idempotent), or make the server include a `since` backfill; with F1 fixed the missed candle is recovered by the batch.

findings.title: Two divergent candle pipelines: engine CandleProjection (per-trade, uncoalesced) is persisted but unconsumed; clients get the API's coalesced aggregation
findings.user_symptom: (3) admin/DB volume disagrees with the app chart
findings.evidence: Engine index.ts:216-226/259-260 wires `candleProjection.onPriceUpdate` per trade (market-state.service.ts:230-233 `this.onPriceUpdate(nextState.battleId, price, now, volumeDelta, 1)`) and :410-427 advanceTimeBucket each second → Redis `active:candle:80:1000`, DB `candles` (300 rows for battle 80, sum 124,545, 69 trades) and channels CANDLE_CLOSED/ACTIVE_UPDATED; grep shows no consumer outside apps/engine and packages/shared. API aggregation for the same battle kept 200 candles, sum 67,520 (F5 window) — same within window here, but diverges whenever F3 drops ticks.
findings.mechanism: Volume shown to traders (API path) can differ from what the engine records as traded notional; maintenance burden of two truths.
findings.fix_sketch: Serve candleBatch/candleClosed from the engine's `candles` table + CANDLE_CLOSED channel (already full-notional, per trade), or delete the engine projection.

chart-motion.area: Trading PWA chart motion & overlays: vertical time cursor ("expiry line"), round-start/end/cooldown transitions, ROUND ENTRY price line, price-scale autoscale (NewChart.jsx + lightweight-charts 5.1.0 + line-chart socket pipeline)
chart-motion.architecture: The chart is a single lightweight-charts 5.1.0 AreaSeries (+ volume Histogram overlay) built in /home/claude/wb/frontend/src/components/NewChart.jsx. TIME AXIS: every bar's `time` is a UNIX SECOND derived from server timestamps (`toChartTime` NewChart.jsx:121-125 floors ms→s); closed candles come from the backend `candleClosed` event whose `timestamp` is the bucket start in seconds (backend apps/api/src/chart/candle-aggregation.ts:92-94, candle-types.ts:42-47); intra-second bars come from main-socket `priceUpdate` ticks (server ms `timestamp`) that useWebSocket.js:1003-1027 forwards into lineChartStore via `upsertLatestCandle`; NewChart rebuilds `rawData` from the store on every store change (`applyStoreToChart` :1291-1370) and appends bars whose second is greater than `lastTimeRef`. The axis is therefore INDEX-based (LWC logical index, no whitespace); a bar exists only when the server delivered a tick or an activity candle: the API suppresses flat (no-activity) candles to clients (apps/api/src/ws/line-chart.gateway.ts:198-206 passes `emitToClients=false`; :396-397 same for gap candles), priceUpdate is dropped while cooldown UI is exclusive (useWebSocket.js:964), and the engine emits no ticks between battles (order-driven engine, battle-engine.service.ts:609). So during the 30 s cooldown (system_settings cooldown_time=30) nothing is appended and the cooldown has ZERO width on the x-axis; the local clock is never used for bar placement. VIEWPORT: `shiftVisibleRangeOnNewBar:true`, `rightOffset:18` (:864-868). Every "full reset" (`applyFullSeriesReset` :1264-1289) does `setData(all)` then `applyDefaultChartZoom` (:256-279) = `timeScale().setVisibleRange(last min(80,n) bars)` + `applyOptions({rightOffset:18})` + price scale `setAutoScale(false)` + manual `setVisibleRange(min/max of those bars ±16%)`. Full resets happen: whenever effect-3 re-runs (deps `[api, activeBattleId, serverHistoryReady, chartEngineReady]` :1497) — i.e. at battleEnd (battleId→null), newBattleStarted (battleId→id), and every `markServerHistoryReady` (candleBatch); when store data is older/newer than the current series (:1327-1329); and 2 s after any pointer/wheel interaction (:955-975). Autoscale is re-enabled only when the store path appends a new bar (:1364-1368). TIME CURSOR: a DOM `<div class="chart-expiry-line">` + tag, positioned every requestAnimationFrame by a hand-built linear map (`seedExpiryMap` :412-422, `expiryXFromMap` :432-439): x = pixel of the newest CLOSED/appended bar (`timeToCoordinate`) + plotOffset + (clamp((Date.now-anchored perf clock − barTime)/1000, 0, 1) + 1)·`barSpacing`, written as translateX (:444-459) when it moved ≥0.05 px (:1124). It is NOT placed at the round's end time: `resolveExpiryReferenceSec` (:748-772) only gates visibility (:1501-1504). ROUND ENTRY: a native `series.createPriceLine` at `Battle.start_price` (:1190-1222) plus a DOM label whose y is synced per frame (:1136-1147). Backend feeds: /line-chart namespace, client always joins scope "all" room (useWebSocket.js:149, gateway joinAll), receives `candleBatch` on (re)subscribe = last 3 COMPLETED battles capped at 200 points (gateway buildCandleBatchPayload) and on every new battle (`broadcastCandleBatchOnNewBattle`).

findings.title: Every 1 Hz timer tick (and every 250 ms snapshot) launches heavy Prisma/projection work on the single broadcaster event loop that also paces the timer

On top, every 250 ms battleSnapshot flush runs `emitPersonalizedToBattleRoom` (ws.gateway.ts:400-437): `await this.server.in(room).fetchSockets()` then per socket `await personalize(...)` (battle.service.ts:1353-1383 → :1337-1348 `getFreeTapsPerUser()` + Redis GET per user) and `remote.emit(event, personalized)` — with the Redis adapter (redis-io.adapter.ts:29-33, :58-60) each RemoteSocket emit is a separate encode + Redis PUBLISH — and then `.finally(() => emitReadModelSyncAfterSnapshot)` (redis.subscriber.ts:~2575-2585) → battle.service.ts:2986-2994 `emitTopTradersUpdate(battleId, { force: true })` which bypasses its throttle (:2963-2969 `if (!opts?.force && …) return;`) and runs the leaderboard raw SQL every 250 ms. The timer forward itself is a `setTimeout` (redis.subscriber.ts:1182) and therefore inherits all of this loop's lag.
findings.mechanism: Under load (many sockets, NPC flow producing a snapshot every 250 ms and thousands of price_ticks rows per round), the broadcaster's loop is saturated by JSON encoding per socket, Redis publishes per socket, Prisma result materialization of full-battle price_ticks several times per second, and per-user projections. The timer dispatcher's setTimeout fires late → wire gaps >1 s → queue depth >1 → catch-up mode at 250 ms → the FE shows freeze-then-jump. Prisma pool contention (local DATABASE_URL has no connection_limit → Prisma default; code comments assume 5) adds latency to the REST estimator calls (E1) and to `balanceEquityAndPnL`.
findings.fix_sketch: (a) Remove the per-tick trade-stream refresh from forwardTimerNow; drive `trade:active:stream` from price/trade changes only, and make the projection cache key coarse (rounded price bucket + pots) with TTL ≥ 1 s. (b) Compute ONE `computeLiveProjectedSettlementPayouts` per (battle, price bucket) per second in the API and share it across dashboard, trade-stream, balance-snapshot and the market-flip/estimate REST handlers (e.g. a small in-memory memo keyed by battleId|priceBucket|potSig with 500-1000 ms TTL). (c) Bound `priceTick.findMany` (downsample server-side, or keep a per-battle in-memory ring of price points fed by the price.tick subscriber). (d) Stop personalizing battleSnapshot per socket every 250 ms: broadcast the shared snapshot once to the room and send `free_taps_left` as a separate per-user event only when it changes. (e) Drop the `force:true` top-traders SQL from the snapshot flush (respect `topTraderEmitThrottleMs`). (f) Longer term: move WS broadcasting to its own process (apps/api/src/ws-service exists) so HTTP/REST projections cannot delay timer emits.

findings.title: Broadcaster leader lease can silently drop every timer/price/snapshot forward for up to ~13 s after an event-loop stall
findings.user_symptom: (1) timer stuck for several seconds then jumps
findings.evidence: ws-broadcaster-leader.service.ts:17-23 `LEADER_TTL_SEC … '10'`, `LEADER_RENEW_MS … '3000'`; :76-78 `this.renewTimer = setInterval(() => { … }, LEADER_RENEW_MS)`; :146-165 on renew failure `this.isLeader = false; this.logger.warn('WS broadcaster leader lost — renewing failed'); await this.tryAcquire();`. redis.subscriber.ts:543-549: `if (skipRedisParseOnNonBroadcaster() && ENGINE_WS_BROADCAST_CHANNELS.has(channel) && !this.shouldBroadcast()) { return; }` (default true, api-load-profile.env.ts:44-49).

findings.fix_sketch: Renew from a lightweight path (unref'd interval is fine) but treat a lost lease on a single-instance deployment as non-fatal: keep forwarding when `PUBSUB NUMSUB` shows one subscriber / when `instances:1`, and log loudly. Check production API logs for 'WS broadcaster leader lost' to confirm or rule out.

findings.title: Market Flip fetch loop invalidates in-flight responses on every pot tick and holds new verdicts 1.5 s — under NPC flow the LOSING state can take seconds or never update
findings.user_symptom: (2) estimator takes seconds to realise the user is losing / show flip numbers
findings.evidence: frontend/src/live/hooks/useMarketFlip.js:52-98: `const requestId = ++requestIdRef.current;` runs on EVERY effect re-run (deps `[battleId, potSignature, priceSignature, enabled]`), and the response is discarded if anything changed since: :72 `.then((res) => { if (requestId !== requestIdRef.current) return; setData(res ?? null);`; each dispatch also aborts the previous request :65 `abortRef.current?.abort();`; the 250 ms trailing debounce (:96 `setTimeout(dispatch, MARKET_FLIP_DEBOUNCE_MS)`) is restarted by every re-run and only the 1500 ms ceiling (:91-94) forces a dispatch. The trigger rate is per-dollar: WinEstimatorSheet.jsx:138-141 `potSignature = \`${Math.round(Number(buyPot) || 0)}:${Math.round(Number(sellPot) || 0)}\``; pots reach the store on every forwarded snapshot whose pots changed (battleSnapshotApplyService.js:36-46 `potsChanged || now - last >= SNAPSHOT_THROTTLE_MS`; server gap 250 ms). DB shows NPC-dominated pots (battle 81: buyPot 203,695 vs sellPot 3,160) so pots move on essentially every snapshot. After a LOSING response lands, WinEstimatorSheet.jsx:235-268 holds it: :20 `VERDICT_DAMP_MS = 1500` … :261 `const timer = setTimeout(() => { … setShownVerdict(...) }, VERDICT_DAMP_MS)`. Server: battle.service.ts:2446-2597 `marketFlip` awaits battle row, Redis stakes, `resolveLiveCurrentPrice` (:315-332), pots, NPC flag, then :2527 `estimateFlipProfit` → battle-payout.estimate.ts:117+ `buildPayoutInputs` (stakes, NPC trades, battle, fee, rpcUser, full `priceTick.findMany`) + `computePayouts`.
findings.mechanism: Chain from a price crossing: engine price.tick → API 200 ms coalesce (redis.subscriber.ts:218-220, :880-925) → client 50 ms throttle (pricePipeline.js:24-37) → `priceSignature` sign flips → effect re-run. From then on, with pots ticking every ~250-500 ms, the debounce never matures, a request goes out only at the 1500 ms ceiling, and its response is accepted only if it returns before the NEXT pot tick (~250 ms). Best case ≈ 200+50+RTT+1500 ≈ 2-2.5 s before the grid appears; with REST latency above the inter-tick gap (Prisma pool shared with T2's hot paths) every response is thrown away and the row keeps showing the previous verdict or 'Updating…' indefinitely — worst case zero accepted responses, invisible in rate-limit metrics. The same requestId pattern exists in useWinEstimate.js:48-57 (scenario cards) with a 200 ms debounce and no ceiling at all.
findings.fix_sketch: In useMarketFlip: (1) keep `requestId` per DISPATCH, not per effect run — increment it inside `dispatch()` and only abort/discard when a newer request has actually been sent; (2) accept the latest completed response and use a leading+trailing throttle (e.g. fetch at most every 750 ms, always fire immediately on a `priceSignature` SIGN change since that is the verdict flip) instead of a starvable trailing debounce; (3) quantize `potSignature` (e.g. 0.5 % of total pot) so NPC churn doesn't retrigger; (4) drop or shorten `VERDICT_DAMP_MS` to ~300 ms once the server adds a pip deadband (the damper only exists because battle.service.ts:2503-2515 uses a bare sign test). Better still: push the verdict over the socket — the server already computes the user's projected side and payout per tick in `trade:active:stream`/`equityAndPnL` (`projected_winner_side`, redis.subscriber.ts:~1382-1400); add `net_side`, `distance_pips`, `volume_required` and `flip_profit` to that per-user frame (computed from the shared projection in T2) and render Market Flip from the store with no REST round-trip.

findings.title: Perpetual 60 fps rAF loops run for the whole round even when nothing changes (pool-bar smoothing, telemetry frame monitor, chart)
findings.user_symptom: (1) freezes/jank on mobile

findings.title: Client stale-watchdog force-reconnects every client after ~10-12 s without data, amplifying server load exactly when the broadcaster is slow
findings.user_symptom: (1) timer stuck then everything reloads; server load spikes
findings.evidence: useWebSocket.js:1399-1424 `startSocketHealthWatchdog({ … onStale: () => { forceReconnectAndSync(); forceLineChartSync(); }, intervalMs: 2000, staleThresholdMs: 5000 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 1000), requiredConsecutiveStaleChecks: 2, minRecoveryGapMs: 9000 })`; socketHealthService.js:15-48 setInterval + `onStale()`. findings.title: Scenario-card estimate fires a POST /battle/estimate-payout (two projections server-side) on every $1 pot move while the sheet is open
findings.user_symptom: (2) estimator load / latency

findings.fix_sketch: Quantize potSignature (≥0.5 % of total pot), throttle to ≤1 req/s, fix the requestId invalidation as in E1, and serve estimates from the shared per-battle projection memo (T2 fix b).

findings.title: Timestamp-ordering guard can drop engine timer ticks after the API-stamped battle.started tick when host clocks are skewed
findings.user_symptom: (1) timer stuck at round start

Client realtimeEventGuards.js:19-28 `if (prev != null && ts < prev) return true;` keyed by event name ('timerUpdate'), cleared only on battle switch (battleSnapshotTransitionService.js:37-40).

findings.fix_sketch: Stamp the synthesized tick with the engine's `payload.timestamp` (available from battle.started), or compare on a monotonic per-battle sequence instead of wall clock; at minimum tolerate ≤2 s of backwards skew for 'timerUpdate'.

findings.title: Timer ticks are discarded while the client has no battle id (after cooldown reset) until a snapshot arrives

findings.fix_sketch: When `activeBattleId == null` accept the tick and adopt its battle_id (or set battleIdRef from `timerUpdate.battle_id` when the store has none).

engine-perf.architecture: A single plain ts-node process (/home/claude/wb/backend/apps/engine/src/index.ts, PM2 "TickTrade-engine", fork/1 instance) wires everything by hand. EngineLeaderService (Redis SET NX, TTL 10 s, renew every 3 s) decides who runs the "leader runtime": BattleStateRecoveryService, BattleEngineService.onModuleInit(), and a 1 s candle-bucket setInterval. BattleEngineService.startEngine() caches the ACTIVE battle row in memory and starts a setInterval(1000) → publishTimerHeartbeat(): remaining is DERIVED each tick as durationSeconds − floor((Date.now() − startTimeMs)/1000) (not decremented), missed seconds are backfilled, the timer payload (~236 B) is fire-and-forget PUBLISHed on 'engine:events:timer', then two fire-and-forget heavy publishers run on the same tick: BattleSnapshotPublisher.publish (Redis MULTI for free-tap+pot hash, 4 more Redis reads incl. full ZRANGE of both leaderboard user sets, 30–60 s DB caches) and RiskTerminalTickPublisher.publish (in-flight guarded; per second: LRANGE of the whole stakes buffer + whole npc-trade buffer, priceTick.findMany of ALL ticks of the battle, battle.findUnique ×2, rpcUser.findMany of ALL rows, sync projection, JSON.stringify ×2, PUBLISH + SET). FINALIZE/settlement checks are deferred via setImmediate (runFinalizeAndSettlementCheck → finishBattle → stop() timer → battle.update CLOSE → PUBLISH battle.end → BullMQ enqueue battle-settlement). The settlement-worker process runs settleBattle (flush Redis buffers → 30 s Prisma tx) and PUBLISHes settlement.completed; the engine's SettlementCompletedListener is the ONLY trigger for the next round (cooldown 30.5 s → createNewBattle → startEngine). Trades reach the engine via Redis pub/sub 'engine:events:trade.executed' (from API/engine-worker BullMQ consumers with concurrency 48, and from npc-worker); RedisCommandSubscriber → BattleEngineService.recalcPriceFromTrade → TradeExecutedHandler.handle → MarketStateService.applyTradeExecuted (in-memory write-through cache + Redis SET market:state:N, publish market.state.updated, fire-and-forget candle update) → price.tick (200 ms coalesce, dropping) → snapshot (250 ms coalesce). All Redis traffic except subscribers and BullMQ goes through ONE shared ioredis connection (redis.client.ts getSharedCommandRedis, maxRetriesPerRequest 5). Prisma pool is 30 conns / 30 s pool_timeout. Equity publishing is disabled by default (ENGINE_MEMORY_FIRST on). The "engine-worker" entry (apps/api/src/engine-worker/main.ts) is NOT the battle engine: it is a NestJS context hosting the trade-command / NPC-avatar / email BullMQ consumers that feed trade.executed into the engine.

findings.title: Concurrent trade.executed handling loses price updates (lost-update race on market state)
findings.user_symptom: Price/chart lags or 'jumps back' under bursts; settlement final price and roundHigh/Low can omit trades' impact; instability under RPC load
findings.evidence: redis.subscriber.ts L93-97: `this.redis.on('message', async (channel, message) => { ... await this.battleEngine.recalcPriceFromTrade(payload); ... })` — one async handler per message, nothing serializes them. market-state.service.ts L143 `const state = await this.repo.get(payload.battleId);` … L151 `const freezeSeconds = await this.configCache.getFreezeSeconds();` … L177 compute from `state.lastPrice` … L214 `await this.repo.set(nextState);`. Producer side: apps/api/src/trades/trade-command.env.ts L23 `TRADE_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY || '48'` — up to 48 trades published concurrently; npc-worker also publishes on the same channel.
findings.mechanism: ioredis emits every 'message' in one synchronous loop per socket read. Handler A yields at its first await; handler B starts and reads the SAME cached state (A has not called repo.set yet). Both compute price/pressure/version from the pre-A state; B's repo.set overwrites A's. A's price impact, pot totals, lastSequence and lastProcessedEventId are lost. Money-affecting because ticktrade:price:last (settlement final price) and roundHigh/roundLow derive from this path.
findings.fix_sketch: Serialize per battle: in RedisCommandSubscriber (or TradeExecutedHandler) push payloads onto a per-battle promise chain / async queue and process strictly FIFO (one in flight). Keep the queue bounded and drop only publishes, never state updates. Alternatively make applyTradeExecuted synchronous between get and set (read freezeSeconds from a sync cache, do repo.set's cache write before any await — the Redis SET can stay async).

findings.title: finishBattle stops the timer before doing fallible I/O; any failure leaves the engine permanently idle with no round
findings.user_symptom: Timer freezes at 0/1 s and never recovers until the process is restarted
findings.evidence: battle-engine.service.ts L1085 `this.stop();` (clears setInterval, nulls activeBattleCache) executes BEFORE L1095-1098 `await this.prisma.battle.update({ where: { id: battleId }, data: updateData })`, L1109 `await this.events.battleEnd(...)`, L1122 `await this.settlementQueue.enqueue(...)`. The only error handling is L918-928 in publishTimerHeartbeat: `.catch((err) => { console.error(`[BattleEngine] runFinalizeAndSettlementCheck failed ...`) })`. `finally` at L1153-1156 just clears finishingBattles. No retry, no watchdog; the battle row stays ACTIVE/FINALIZE so nothing in-process ever revisits it.
findings.mechanism: Under DB contention (P2024 pool timeout — the pool is shared with the per-second candle upsert and risk-terminal queries) or a Redis blip (enqueue on a maxRetriesPerRequest:null connection can also hang forever), finishBattle throws after the timer is already cleared. No battle.end, no settlement job, no settlement.completed, no next battle. Only a process restart (BattleStateRecoveryService) heals it.
findings.fix_sketch: Do not call stop() until battle.end and the enqueue have succeeded (or move stop() after enqueue and keep the heartbeat idempotent while state==='CLOSE'). Wrap finishBattle in a bounded retry with backoff; on final failure publish battle.end anyway and schedule a recovery attempt (setTimeout) instead of dropping to idle. Add an in-process watchdog: if activeBattleId is null and no createNewBattle timer is pending for > cooldown+N s, run recoverBeforeEngineStart + start().

findings.title: Next round depends solely on settlement.completed pub/sub; a failed settlement job can never be re-enqueued (BullMQ jobId dedupe)
findings.user_symptom: After a round ends nothing starts; timer stuck; restarting the engine does not help while the failed job exists
findings.evidence: battle-engine.service.ts L1227-1242 scheduleNextBattleAfterSettlement is the only caller of createNewBattle after a finish; settlement-completed.listener.ts L31-45 is plain pub/sub (at-most-once). settlement-queue.producer.ts L18-22 attempts 3, backoff 1 s exp; L47-48 `removeOnFail: { age: 86_400, count: 500 }`; L61-63 `jobId: `battle-${payload.battleId}``. battle-state-recovery.service.ts L97-100 re-enqueues with the same payload/jobId. BullMQ addStandardJob-8.lua L90-93: `if rcall("EXISTS", jobIdKey) == 1 then return handleDuplicatedJob(...)` — add is ignored while the job hash exists (failed jobs are kept 24 h). settlement-worker: SETTLEMENT_TX_TIMEOUT_MS 30 s (battle-settlement.service.ts L125-131).
findings.mechanism: If settlement fails all 3 attempts (tx timeout under load), or the settlement.completed message is dropped because the engine's subscriber connection was reconnecting, no next battle is ever created. Recovery's re-enqueue is a silent no-op for 24 h because the failed job with id battle-N still exists.
findings.fix_sketch: (a) Engine-side fallback timer: after enqueue, arm a setTimeout (e.g. 90 s) that polls battles.status; if still not COMPLETED, re-enqueue (with a fresh jobId or after `queue.remove`/`job.retry()`), and if COMPLETED but no event was seen, call scheduleNextBattleAfterSettlement directly. (b) In healPendingSettlements, fetch the job by id; if state is 'failed' call job.retry() (or remove then add). (c) Consider making next-round creation independent of settlement (create the new battle after battle.end; let settlement finish in the background) so a slow settlement never freezes the game.

findings.title: Risk-terminal tick does unbounded Postgres + Redis reads and O(trades) CPU every second on the engine loop
findings.user_symptom: Event-loop stalls → skipped/backfilled timer seconds, delayed snapshots, growing DB pool pressure as a round fills up
findings.evidence: battle-engine.service.ts L864-874 fires `this.riskTerminalTickPublisher.publish(cache.id, remaining)` every heartbeat. risk-terminal-tick.publisher.ts L82 `await this.prisma.battle.findUnique(...)`, L84 `await buildDirectiveRoundInput(...)` → packages/shared/src/npc-organic/round-context.ts L161-185: `listBufferedStakes` (LRANGE 0 -1 of the whole stakes buffer, battle-stake-buffer.ts L83), `listBufferedNpcTrades` (LRANGE 0 -1), `prisma.priceTick.findMany({ where: { battleId }, orderBy: [...] })` (ALL ticks of the round), `prisma.battle.findUnique`, `prisma.rpcUser.findMany({ select: { linkedUserId: true } })` (ALL rows, every second). Legacy model path: battle-payout.live.ts L145-160 + L377-425 → 3× LRANGE stakes + 3× LRANGE npc + 2 DB queries per tick. Context refresh every 5 s: npcRoundAudit.findUnique + Redis GET×2 (+ systemSetting.findMany on miss). Observed in redis MONITOR (6 s): engine client 127.0.0.1:57936 issued LRANGE ticktrade:battle:83:stakes:buffer and …npc_trades:buffer once per second; payload 1295 B published + SET. price_ticks is written once per priced trade by the API (redis.subscriber.ts L255-258), so its size is O(trades/round).
findings.mechanism: With thousands of trades per round the per-second work becomes: parse thousands of JSON lines from two LRANGEs, load thousands of price_tick rows through Prisma, scan all rpc_users, run projectDirectiveScenarios over all of it, stringify twice. All of that is synchronous CPU on the same event loop that must fire the 1 s heartbeat; the in-flight guard (L60-68) prevents pile-up but not the stall. Two heavy DB queries/second also compete with finishBattle and candle upserts for the 30-conn pool.
findings.fix_sketch: Move the risk-terminal projection off the heartbeat and out of the engine process (admin-only consumer; compute it in the API on demand or on a 5 s cadence in a separate worker). If it stays: cache rpcUser ids (TTL 60 s), keep an incremental in-memory round input (append stakes/npc trades/ticks as they arrive, maintain high/low incrementally) instead of re-reading everything, cap price ticks (only high/low/last are needed — roundHigh/Low already live in market state), and only publish when inputs changed.

findings.title: Snapshot publisher reads both full leaderboard user ZSETs (ZRANGE 0 -1) up to 5×/s just to count members
findings.user_symptom: Heartbeat/snapshot latency grows linearly with number of traders; event-loop stalls with many users
findings.evidence: battle-snapshot.publisher.ts L282-287: `Promise.all([ listBattleLeaderboardUserIds(r, battleId), r.zcard(...BUY...), r.zcard(...SELL...), r.get(battleLockKey(battleId)) ])`; L288 uses only `userIds.length`. packages/shared/src/redis/battle-leaderboard.ts L58-61: `redis.zrange(battleLeaderboardUserKey(battleId,'BUY'), 0, -1)` + SELL, then builds a Set. Callers: heartbeat every second (battle-engine.service.ts L849-858), every coalesced trade follow-up (trade-executed.handler.ts L302, 250 ms → up to 4/s), free-tap commands. MONITOR: zrange lb:battle:83:buy/sell from engine ports 57936/57928 8× and 2× in 6 s.
findings.mechanism: O(N users) reply transfer + JS parsing + Set construction per call on the engine event loop and the single shared Redis connection, purely to get a distinct count.
findings.fix_sketch: Maintain a per-battle 'distinct traders' SET (SADD on stake write; SCARD here), or ZUNIONSTORE into a temp key + ZCARD, or cache traderCount for 1 s and refresh asynchronously. Never ZRANGE 0 -1 on a hot path.

findings.title: Timer publish shares one Redis connection with all heavy traffic and any publish rejection crashes the process (no unhandledRejection handler)
findings.user_symptom: Timer ticks arrive late/bunched under load; engine dies (PM2 restart storm, max_restarts 10) during Redis blips
findings.evidence: redis.client.ts L84-93 `getSharedCommandRedis()` returns one ioredis instance used by RedisPublisher, RedisStateService, MarketStateRepository, CandleStoreService, BattlePotCache, battle.state.ts, leaderboard reads; L70 `maxRetriesPerRequest: 5`. battle-engine.service.ts L831 `void this.events.timerUpdate({...})` → battle-events.publisher.ts L63-65 → redis.publisher.ts L6-8 `await this.redis.publish(event, JSON.stringify(payload))` — no .catch. Same for L798 backfill loop. grep for unhandledRejection/uncaughtException in apps/engine/src and packages/shared/src: none. Node v22 (default --unhandled-rejections=throw). ecosystem.config.js L23-25 autorestart, max_restarts 10, restart_delay 3000.
findings.mechanism: (a) Head-of-line: the PUBLISH is written behind pending LRANGE/ZRANGE commands on the same socket and its reply is parsed after theirs; large replies delay both the write buffer drain and loop availability. (b) When Redis is briefly unreachable, after 5 retries every queued command rejects; the un-caught `void timerUpdate` rejection throws at process level → engine exits → PM2 restarts (≤10 times) → each restart re-runs recovery and overwrites market state (see F7).
findings.fix_sketch: Give the timer its own dedicated ioredis connection (and ideally its own tiny scheduler process/module) so it is never queued behind bulk reads. Wrap every fire-and-forget publish in .catch (timerUpdate, backfill, tradePriced already ok). Register process.on('unhandledRejection') that logs and keeps the process alive, and consider maxRetriesPerRequest: null + command timeout for publishers so transient blips degrade instead of crash.

findings.title: Leader election drops leadership on any Redis error, restarting the runtime and overwriting live market state with stale DB pots
findings.user_symptom: Timer disappears for ≥3 s then restarts; pots/high-low shown by risk terminal reset mid-round; synthetic price tick on chart
findings.evidence: engine-leader.service.ts L176-183: `catch (err) { this.isLeader = false; console.warn('[EngineLeader] renew failed', ...) } this.notifyLeadership(wasLeader);` → index.ts L468-474 `engineLeader.onLeadershipChange((isLeader) => { if (isLeader) void startLeaderRuntime(); else void stopLeaderRuntime(); })` → L461 `await battleEngine.onModuleDestroy()` → stop() clears the interval. Re-acquire 3 s later (L173-174) → startLeaderRuntime → recoverBeforeEngineStart + onModuleInit → start() → startEngine. startEngine L661-677: `const existingState = await this.marketStateRepo.get(battle.id); const pressure = existingState ? ... : 0; const state = buildInitialMarketState(battle.id, Number(battle.startPrice), Number(battle.buyPot ?? 0), Number(battle.sellPot ?? 0), initialPrice, ...); await this.marketStateRepo.set(state);` — unconditional overwrite; battles.buyPot/sellPot are 0 mid-round (DB row updated only at settlement — confirmed: battle 83 ACTIVE shows 0.00/0.00 while Redis pot hash carries live totals); buildInitialMarketState resets roundHigh=roundLow=price, lastProcessedEventId=null, version=1. L653 `await this.publishPriceAndChart(battle.id, initialPrice, 0, 0, 0)` publishes source:'trade' tick and a candle update. Also index.ts L381-383/456-466: stopLeaderRuntime has no guard against an in-flight startLeaderRuntime (leaderRuntimeStarting), so stop→start interleaving can leave a timer running in a non-leader.
findings.mechanism: A single failed EVAL (Redis reconnect, timeout) flips isLeader false even in single-instance deployments; the resulting stop/start cycle kills the 1 Hz timer, re-runs recovery queries, and clobbers market:state (risk-terminal pots read from it; roundHigh/roundLow later written to battles at finishBattle L1089-1098 and used by settlement).
findings.fix_sketch: In tick(): on a Redis error keep leadership until the key is observed to be held by someone else or TTL has provably elapsed (track lastRenewOk; only drop after TTL). In startEngine: if existingState exists, keep it (only patch status/freezeState) — mirror BattleStateRecoveryService.ensureMarketStateHydrated, which already only creates when missing; never reset pots from the DB row mid-round. Make startLeaderRuntime/stopLeaderRuntime mutually exclusive (await the in-flight start before stopping). Set ENGINE_SINGLE_INSTANCE=1 where only one engine runs.

findings.title: Candle bucket timer does a Postgres upsert every second with no in-flight guard; per-trade candle RMW is unserialized
findings.user_symptom: Constant DB write load competing with settlement; overlapping upserts under contention; candle volume/tick counts under-reported in bursts
findings.evidence: index.ts L411-427 `candleBucketTimerId = setInterval(async () => { ... await candleProjection.advanceTimeBucket(activeBattleId, Date.now()); ... }, 1000)` — no re-entrancy flag. candle-projection.service.ts L33-36 `getActive` (Redis GET) → `await this.store.finalizeToDb(active)` → candle-store.service.ts L44 `await this.prisma.candle.upsert(...)` → L66 setActive (Redis SET) → publish. DB: 300 candle rows per 300 s battle (flat continuity candles). engine.log: `[engine][slow_query] ms=358 ... INSERT INTO "public"."candles" ... ON CONFLICT` observed with no load. market-state.service.ts L230-233 `void this.onPriceUpdate(nextState.battleId, price, now, volumeDelta, 1)` per trade → onPriceUpdate L82 GET active → L95 SET (read-modify-write) with no serialization.
findings.mechanism: One Postgres write per second per engine regardless of activity, holding a pool connection; if an upsert exceeds 1 s, the next interval overlaps (two finalizeToDb for the same bucket, two SETs). Concurrent per-trade candle updates read the same active candle and overwrite each other, losing volume/tickCount.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep the active candle in memory (single writer), batch-flush closed candles to Postgres asynchronously (e.g. createMany every 5 s or at round end), add an in-flight guard to the bucket timer, and serialize onPriceUpdate through the same per-battle queue as F1.

findings.title: Next round start is serialized behind settlement (worst case ~95 s) and the NPC align-at-close wait
findings.user_symptom: Long dead time after 0 s before the next round; 'settling' hangs when the settlement worker is slow
findings.evidence: battle-engine.service.ts L1067-1076 awaits beforeBattleClose (index.ts L310-322 polls Redis every 50 ms up to NPC_ALIGN_AT_CLOSE_WAIT_MS = 2000 ms) BEFORE battle.end at L1109. Next round: L1240-1241 `const delayMs = await this.resolveCreateNextBattleDelayMs('finish'); setTimeout(() => void this.createNewBattle(), delayMs);` only from SettlementCompletedListener. settlement-queue.producer.ts attempts 3 / backoff 1 s exp; battle-settlement.service.ts L125-131 tx timeout 30 s; settlement-worker log locally: totalMs 78–116 with ~100 npc trades (flushMs ~40, txMs ~50). cooldown_status=enable, cooldown_time=30 → +30.5 s after settlement.completed.
findings.mechanism: Gap = align wait (≤2 s) + settlement duration (grows with stakes/npc trades/price ticks: flush + tx reads all stakes, npc_trades, price_ticks) + cooldown. A 30 s tx timeout × 3 attempts plus backoff delays the next round by up to ~1.5 min, and a final failure → F3 (never).
findings.fix_sketch: Decouple: create the next battle on a wall-clock schedule anchored to battle.end (cooldown from end, not from settlement.completed) and let settlement run concurrently; make the cooldown UI on the API also anchor to battle.end. Keep settlement.completed only for battleEndDetails. Persist the anchor in Redis so failover honours it.

findings.title: price.tick coalescer drops the last tick of a burst instead of deferring it; heartbeat never re-publishes price
findings.user_symptom: Chart price lags the real last price until the next trade; 'delayed updates' during/after bursts
findings.evidence: events/price-tick-coalesce.ts L12-19: `if (now - last < PRICE_TICK_COALESCE_MS) return false;` — caller trade-executed.handler.ts L276-300 simply skips publishing; no trailing-edge timer. `source: 'heartbeat'` exists in PriceTickOpts (battle-events.publisher.ts L4,L12) but publishTimerHeartbeat never publishes a price tick. Same pattern in trade-snapshot-coalesce.ts (mitigated by the 1 s heartbeat snapshot).
findings.mechanism: Within a 200 ms window only the first tick is published; the final price of the window is lost from the WS stream (market:state Redis key is correct, but no consumer re-reads it).
findings.fix_sketch: Trailing-edge coalescing: remember the latest pending tick and flush it with a setTimeout at window end; or have the heartbeat publish the current market-state price once per second when it differs from the last published tick (source:'heartbeat', changed:false).

findings.title: Per-battle Redis keys are never expired or deleted (market:state, active:candle, chart:history:completed)
findings.user_symptom: Slow Redis memory/key growth over days; not an immediate timer cause
findings.evidence: redis-cli: market:state:80..83 TTL -1 (market-state.repository.ts L68 `set(key, JSON)` no EX; forget() L78-80 clears memory only); active:candle:80..83:1000 TTL -1 (candle-store.service.ts L36); chart:history:completed:81/82 TTL -1, 200 members, ~43 KB each (written by apps/api/src/ws/line-chart.gateway.ts). 96 keys / 2.76 MB now after 84 battles on a fresh DB.
findings.mechanism: ~288 rounds/day → ~12 MB/day from chart history alone plus small strings; unbounded.
findings.fix_sketch: Set EX (e.g. 24 h) on market:state and active:candle writes; DEL/EXPIRE them in scheduleNextBattleAfterSettlement/cancel alongside forgetBattle; add TTL to chart:history:completed in the API.

findings.title: Equity fan-out (if enabled) is O(users) uncapped concurrency with per-user full-buffer LRANGE and DB queries
findings.user_symptom: Only if ENGINE_EQUITY_PUBLISH_ON_TRADE / ENGINE_HEAVY_PUBLISH_ON_CHART_TICK are enabled in prod: massive per-trade load
findings.evidence: engine-hot-path.env.ts L20-30: both default off when ENGINE_MEMORY_FIRST (default on). equity-pnl.publisher.ts L129-137 `Promise.allSettled(realUserIds.map((userId) => this.publishForUser(...)))` no cap; equity-pnl.service.ts L57-64 stake.findMany per user, L74-86 `battle.findFirst` + `listBufferedStakes` (LRANGE whole buffer) per user, L195-202 priceTick.findFirst per battle per user.
findings.mechanism: N users × (2–3 DB queries + full LRANGE + JSON parse) per trigger, all concurrent → pool exhaustion (P2024) that also starves finishBattle (F2).
findings.fix_sketch: Keep disabled; if needed, compute one projection per battle (already done) and derive per-user PnL from the buffered stake list once (no per-user queries), publish via one batched message, cap concurrency.

findings.title: Heartbeat timer value is correctly deadline-derived; residual cadence issues are minor
findings.user_symptom: Occasional duplicate second or phase jitter; isFinalize false on the first ticks after a cold start
findings.evidence: battle-engine.service.ts L767-772 `const now = Date.now(); const elapsed = Math.max(0, Math.floor((now - cache.startTimeMs) / 1000)); const remaining = Math.max(0, cache.durationSeconds - elapsed);` (not decremented); L789-812 backfill; L680-682 `setInterval(() => { void this.publishTimerHeartbeat(); }, TIMER_HEARTBEAT_MS)`; L827-829 emits whenever remaining>0 even if equal to lastPublishedRemaining; L779-784 `freezeCached = ... : this.cachedFreezeSeconds ?? 0` when the cache was never primed; L760-761/935 heartbeatRunning guard is vacuous (no awaits inside).
findings.mechanism: setInterval phase drifts relative to the second boundary of startTimeMs, so a value can be published twice and the next skipped-then-backfilled; harmless but noisy for the API pacer (250 ms catch-up). No dead-loop error path in the heartbeat itself.
findings.fix_sketch: Use a self-rescheduling setTimeout aligned to (startTimeMs + k*1000 + small offset) so each firing lands just after the boundary; skip emit when remaining === lastPublishedRemaining; prime cachedFreezeSeconds synchronously before starting the interval (await getFreezeSeconds in startEngine).

open_questions: Production env flags are unknown: NPC_SIM_IN_ENGINE / NPC_WORKER_ENABLED (if the 16.8k-line NpcSimulatorService or the organic engine runs inside the engine process, its timers add loop load on top of the above), ENGINE_SINGLE_INSTANCE, ENGINE_EQUITY_PUBLISH_ON_TRADE, ENGINE_HEAVY_PUBLISH_ON_CHART_TICK, LIVE_BATTLE_REDIS_ONLY (default on → LRANGE buffers; off → per-second Postgres findMany on stakes/npc_trades instead).

No engine event-loop-lag warnings were logged locally (0 hits) because there is no load in this environment; the [Engine] event-loop lag p99/max lines from a production log would quantify F4/F5 directly.
engine.log lines carry no timestamps, so timer publish gaps could not be measured from logs; redis MONITOR showed a clean 1.000 s cadence (…105.531, 106.531, 107.531, 108.532, 109.532) at idle.

The API-side timer pacer (apps/api/src/redis/redis.subscriber.ts handleTimer, 250 ms catch-up gap) and the WS broadcaster leader are a second place ticks can be delayed; outside this area but relevant to the owner's symptom.

api-ws-perf.area: backend API + WebSocket fan-out performance/correctness (apps/api/src/ws, redis/redis.subscriber.ts, trades/*, battle/*, common/cooldown)
api-ws-perf.architecture: Single PM2 fork instance (ecosystem.config.js `instances: 1`) runs the NestJS API with three Socket.IO namespaces (`/` WebsocketGateway+BattleGateway, `/line-chart`, `/chat`) behind `@socket.io/redis-adapter` 8.3 (RedisIoAdapter, pub=shared command ioredis, sub=shared subscriber). The engine process publishes battle events to Redis channels (`engine:events:timer|price.tick|battle.snapshot|battle.end|...`, `trade.executed.v1`, `settlement.completed`); `RedisSubscriber` (dedicated ioredis SUBSCRIBE connection) JSON-parses every message, gates on `WsBroadcasterLeaderService.isBroadcasterLeader()` (Redis SET NX lock, TTL 10s, renew 3s) and routes to handlers that coalesce per battle (timer FIFO pacer 1000/250 ms, priceUpdate 200 ms, battleSnapshot 250/120/80 ms) and fan out via `WebsocketGateway.emitToBattle/emitToUser/emitPersonalizedToBattleRoom`. Trades enter via WS `trade:buy|sell` (BattleGateway) or HTTP (TradesController→TradesService.buy→TradeOrderCoalescer), go through `executeOrder`: Redis idempotency claim → (lean default) `TradeFastValidationService.validateLight` + Redis spendable reserve → BullMQ enqueue; the `engine-worker` process (`TradeCommandWorkerService`) runs `executeQueuedTradeJob`→`executeOrderSerialized` (per-(battle,user) FIFO, Prisma interactive tx that in lean mode only reads `battle` and writes Redis: pending-debit hash, stake buffer list, pot hash) then publishes `trade.executed.v1` + `trade.async.result` which the API leader relays to `user_{id}` rooms. `UserBalanceFlushService` (leader, 500 ms) drains Redis pending debits into Postgres `users.balance`. Key files: /home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/ws/ws.gateway.ts, ws/battle.gateway.ts, ws/line-chart.gateway.ts, ws/redis-io.adapter.ts, redis/redis.subscriber.ts, redis/ws-broadcaster-leader.service.ts, trades/trades.service.ts, trades/trade-order-coalescer.ts, trades/user-balance-flush.service.ts, trades/user-spendable-balance.service.ts, engine-worker/trade-command-worker.service.ts, battle/battle.service.ts.

findings.title: Balance flush loses concurrent debits: HGETALL → user.update → DEL is not atomic
findings.user_symptom: Users retain balance they already staked (house loses money); spendable cache re-seeds from an un-debited Postgres balance after TTL
findings.evidence:
/home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/trades/user-balance-flush.service.ts:100-130:
`const raw = await redis.hgetall(key); ... await this.prisma.user.update({ ... balance: { decrement: balanceDec } }); await redis.del(key);`
Producer runs in another process (engine-worker BullMQ job) at /home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/trades/user-spendable-balance.service.ts:139-146: `await redis.hincrbyfloat(pk, 'balanceDec', fromBalance); ... await redis.sadd(DIRTY_USERS_KEY, ...)`. Flush is the default path: trade-hot-path.env.ts:156-164 `redisBalanceAuthorityEnabled()` returns true when `liveBattleRedisOnlyEnabled()` (default true, packages/shared/src/redis/live-battle-redis-only.ts:11-23) and trades.service.ts:2424-2435 skips `tx.user.update` in that mode.
findings.mechanism: Any HINCRBYFLOAT that lands between the flush's HGETALL and its DEL (window = Postgres UPDATE latency, seconds under load; flush loops users sequentially every 500 ms) is deleted without ever being applied to Postgres. Also flushAllDirty (lines 80-90) does SMEMBERS then DEL of the dirty set, so an SADD in between is dropped until the user trades again.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the drain atomic: Lua script that HGETALL+DEL (or RENAME pending → pending:flushing:<uuid>) and returns the values; apply to Postgres; on failure HINCRBYFLOAT the amounts back. Alternatively after a successful update do `HINCRBYFLOAT key balanceDec -balanceDec` instead of DEL and delete only when both fields are 0. Same for the dirty set: use SPOP-based draining, not SMEMBERS+DEL. Files: trades/user-balance-flush.service.ts.

findings.title: rollbackPendingDebit credit is discarded by the flush's Math.max(0, …) clamp → user charged for a rolled-back trade
findings.user_symptom: User balance debited in Postgres for a trade that failed/rolled back and never refunded
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/trades/trades.service.ts:2429-2433 `queuePendingDebit` runs INSIDE the Prisma tx callback; on any later throw the catch at 2676-2682 calls `rollbackPendingDebit`, which does `redis.hincrbyfloat(pk, 'balanceDec', -fromBalance)` (user-spendable-balance.service.ts:165-169). The flush clamps: user-balance-flush.service.ts:103-114 `const balanceDec = Math.max(0, Number(raw.balanceDec ?? 0) || 0); ... if (balanceDec <= 0 && friendsDec <= 0) { await redis.del(key); continue; }`.
findings.mechanism: If the 500 ms leader flush runs between queuePendingDebit and rollbackPendingDebit (tx timeout/`getSpendable` Redis error/`stakeBuffer.append` failure at 2660 all land here), Postgres is decremented, the rollback writes a negative pending value, and the next flush deletes it as "nothing to do". The user is permanently short the stake amount with no stake row.
findings.fix_sketch: Never clamp: apply negative pending values as `balance: { increment }` (or a compensating ledger row). Better: move `queuePendingDebit` out of the tx and only queue after the durable stake write (`stakeBuffer.append` / `tx.stake.create`) has succeeded; keep the Redis reserve (`tryReserve`) as the only pre-commit hold. Files: trades/trades.service.ts (2424-2435, 2659-2674, 2676-2690), trades/user-balance-flush.service.ts.

findings.title: Pending debit + reserve persisted before the stake row: process crash between them loses the order but keeps the debit
findings.user_symptom: After a worker restart under load, users report money taken with no position
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/trades/trades.service.ts:2429 `await this.spendableBalance.queuePendingDebit(...)` (inside tx) vs 2659-2673 `await this.stakeBuffer.append({...})` (after tx, in lean default mode the only durable record of the stake, see 2497-2499 `stakeId = tempStakeId`). No compensation runs on process exit; `rollbackPendingDebit` only runs in the catch block.
findings.mechanism: With LIVE_BATTLE_REDIS_ONLY (default) the stake exists only in the Redis buffer list appended AFTER the debit is queued. A crash (see F6: unhandled rejections crash Node 22) or SIGKILL/PM2 max_memory_restart between 2429 and 2660 leaves a debit that F1's flush applies to Postgres with no stake. Idempotency key stays `pending` (stale after 60 s) so a client retry places a second, fully-charged order.
findings.fix_sketch: Write the stake buffer row and the pending debit in one Redis MULTI (or one Lua) so they are atomic; or append the stake first and queue the debit second with a reconciliation job that matches pending debits to buffered stakes. Files: trades/trades.service.ts.

findings.title: TradeOrderCoalescer drops idempotency keys when merging and double-counts a retried click
findings.user_symptom: Duplicate/over-sized stake when a client retries a click (only if TRADE_COALESCE_ENABLED=true; default off)
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/trades/trade-order-coalescer.ts:115-119 `st.sum += amount; ... if (idempotencyKey) st.idempotencyKeys.push(idempotencyKey);` and 212-213 `const idem = st.idempotencyKeys.length === 1 ? st.idempotencyKeys[0]! : null;` (logged as `idempotencyDiscarded`). The idempotency claim happens only downstream in executeOrder (trades.service.ts:1197-1201), i.e. after merging. HTTP path always goes through the coalescer (trades.service.ts:3894, 3967); enable flag at trade-order-coalescer.ts:280.
findings.mechanism: A client that re-sends the same idempotencyKey within the 100-450 ms window (network retry) has both submissions summed into one stake with NO idempotency key, so neither Redis claim nor `idempotency_records` can dedupe it; two different keys merged likewise lose replay protection for both.
findings.fix_sketch: Dedupe by idempotencyKey inside `submit` (same key → attach waiter to existing part, don't add amount); when >1 distinct keys are merged, derive a deterministic batch key (e.g. sha of sorted keys) and store the result under every constituent key. Files: trades/trade-order-coalescer.ts, trades/trade-idempotency.service.ts.

findings.title: BullMQ worker skips the idempotency claim; a stalled/redelivered job can re-execute or mark a successful trade as failed
findings.user_symptom: User told 'TRADE_LOCK_TIMEOUT'/'failed' while the stake was actually placed → they re-trade → double stake
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/trades/trades.service.ts:1197 `if (idempotencyKey && !execOpts?.worker && !isRpcBot) { claim... }` — worker path (1136-1151) never checks the claim or `tradeCommandResults.get(commandId)`. engine-worker/trade-command-worker.service.ts:145-158: spin lock budget `tradeQueueLockSpinBudgetMs()` = 2000 ms (trade-command.env.ts:28-31) then `results.setFailed(...)` + `publishFailure` + UnrecoverableError. Tx limits trades.service.ts:2599-2602 `maxWait: 15_000/30_000, timeout: 35_000/120_000` exceed BullMQ's default 30 s job lock.
findings.mechanism: If executeOrderSerialized exceeds 30 s (pool wait 15 s + tx up to 35-120 s is allowed), BullMQ marks the job stalled and redelivers it. The second run either (a) times out on the 2 s spin lock and overwrites the command result with 'failed' and emits `trade:async:error` while the first run later succeeds, or (b) acquires the lock after the first run released it and executes the trade again with no idempotency guard.
findings.fix_sketch: In `processJob` read `results.get(commandId)` first and no-op if status is completed/failed; pass `lockDuration` ≥ tx timeout and `maxStalledCount: 0` on the Worker; make the worker path also consult `claimOrGetCached` (status done → return cached). Files: engine-worker/trade-command-worker.service.ts, trades/trades.service.ts:1136-1151.

findings.title: Fire-and-forget async handlers with no catch → unhandled rejection crashes the API process on Node 22 (no process-level handler)
findings.user_symptom: Instability under load: API restarts (PM2), all sockets drop, reconnect storm amplifies DB pool exhaustion
findings.evidence: Node v22.22.2 (`node dist/main.js`, pid 1277, no --unhandled-rejections flag); grep for `unhandledRejection` in apps/api/src, packages/*/src, @nestjs/core, nestjs-pino: none. Unguarded call sites in /home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/redis/redis.subscriber.ts: 706 `this.handleBattleEnd(payload);`, 716 `void this.handleBattleStarted(payload);` (its `await this.prisma.systemSetting.findUnique` at 2648 is outside any try), 737 `this.handleNpcTrade(payload);` (`npcNotificationPauseService.isPaused` at 3158 unguarded), 852 and 1373 `void this.tradesService.emitActiveTradeStreamUpdatesForBattle(...)` (no .catch; its `Promise.all` of 4 Prisma queries at trades.service.ts:4905-4929 rejects with P2024 under pool pressure); trades.service.ts:4875-4882 setTimeout → `void this.emitActiveTradeStreamUpdatesForBattle(...)` no catch.
findings.mechanism: emitActiveTradeStreamUpdatesForBattle runs every timer tick (1 Hz) and after every trade; the first P2024 pool timeout (30 s pool_timeout, connection_limit 30, prisma.service.ts:35-39) that escapes becomes an unhandled rejection and Node terminates the process.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `.catch()` to every `void` promise in redis.subscriber.ts route()/handlers and trades.service.ts scheduling; wrap `route()` dispatch in `Promise.resolve(handler()).catch(log)`; register `process.on('unhandledRejection')` in main.ts as a backstop that logs instead of exiting. Files: redis/redis.subscriber.ts, trades/trades.service.ts, main.ts.

findings.title: Per-connection / per-subscribe DB storm (~50 Prisma queries per client connect; repeated for every client at every new battle)
findings.user_symptom: Delayed updates right after reconnects and at round start; P2024 pool timeouts
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/ws/ws.gateway.ts:272-273 fires `emitCooldownStatusOnConnect` (315-321: getSettings + getActiveBattleId + resolveBootstrapBattleId → 3 findFirst) and `emitBootstrapBattleSnapshotOnConnect` (345-346: 3 more findFirst) + battle.service.ts:539-583 `buildBootstrapBattleSnapshot` (battle.findUnique, getFreeTapData, systemSetting.findUnique, resolveLivePotTotals). ws/battle.gateway.ts `subscribeToBattle` 134-312 runs sequentially: getActiveBattleId, battle.findUnique, bootstrap snapshot again, `engine:commands:battle.join` publish, user.findUnique + `getEquityAndPnlForBalanceEvent` (trades.service.ts:3651-3755: stake.findMany, getActiveBattleId, stake buffer LRANGE, battle.findMany, price query), `getBattleChatMessages` (battle.service.ts:1678-1708: 3 queries incl. COUNT), `getTopTradersForBattle` (2996-3110), `emitTradingDashboardUpdate` TWICE (battle.gateway.ts:298 and 371 via startTradingDashboardStream; each battle.service.ts:2080-2401 ≈ 6 queries incl. `computeLiveProjectedSettlementPayouts`), `getActiveTradesStream` (trades.service.ts:4712-4819). Dedupe at battle.gateway.ts:192-229 only skips the bootstrap snapshot. Client emits subscribeToBattle twice per connect: /home/claude/wb/frontend/src/utils/useWebSocket.js:695 `emitSubscribeToBattle(socket, battleIdForConnect, { includeRange: true })` → 266-270 two emits; no WS rate limit on subscribeToBattle.
findings.mechanism: O(clients) × ~50 queries on every reconnect wave and on every newBattleStarted (all clients resubscribe together) against a 30-connection pool; the trade tx (`maxWait` 15 s) and the 1 Hz stream refresh queue behind them, so everything the user sees is late.
findings.fix_sketch: Cache `getActiveBattleId`/`resolveBootstrapBattleId` and bootstrap snapshot in memory (invalidate on battle.started/end); build chatHistory/topTraders/dashboard once per battle and serve from cache on subscribe; make `subscribeToBattle` dedupe ALL side-effects when already in the room (not just the snapshot) and drop the duplicate `emitTradingDashboardUpdate`; rate-limit subscribeToBattle per socket; on the client send one subscribe. Files: ws/ws.gateway.ts, ws/battle.gateway.ts, battle/battle.service.ts, frontend useWebSocket.js.

findings.title: battleSnapshot fan-out is O(connected sockets) with per-user async personalization at up to 12.5 Hz, plus a top-traders read-model query per flush
findings.user_symptom: Event-loop stalls during trade bursts; timerUpdate/priceUpdate arrive late or bunched
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/redis/redis.subscriber.ts:2429-2438 gap shrinks to 80 ms in the last 25 s; 2557-2584 `emitPersonalizedToBattleRoom(... enrichBattleSnapshotWithUserFreeTaps)` then `.finally(() => emitReadModelSyncAfterSnapshot)`. ws/ws.gateway.ts:410-437 `const sockets = await this.server.in(room).fetchSockets(); ... await Promise.all(sockets.map(async (remote) => { ... personalized = await personalize(...) ... remote.emit(event, personalized); }))` — `personalize` = battle.service.ts:1353-1383 (3 awaits: getFreeTapData, Redis GET, getFreetapBattleFreezeSeconds) per distinct user, and one JSON encode per socket (socket.io broadcast-operator.js:293 returns local Socket, `socket.packet` encodes per socket). `emitReadModelSyncAfterSnapshot` (battle.service.ts:2986-2994) forces `emitTopTradersUpdate` → `getTopTradersForBattle` (2996-3110: resolveRoundBattleIdsForReadModels + battle.findUnique ×2 + Redis ZSETs + user.findMany) on every flush because `SYNC_TOP_TRADERS_WITH_SNAPSHOT` defaults true (266-268). fetchSockets also does a `PUBSUB NUMSUB` Redis round-trip per call (redis-adapter dist/index.js:550,676). handleBattleSnapshot additionally triggers `emitTradingDashboardToBattleParticipants` every 500 ms (2513-2525; ≈6 queries per participant, unbounded `Promise.allSettled` at battle.service.ts:2039-2043) and the balance snapshot every 1 s (2530).
findings.mechanism: Every snapshot flush costs N encodes + U×3 awaits + 5-6 DB/Redis reads for top traders + participant dashboards; at 2000 sockets and 12 Hz this saturates the single event loop and the DB pool, and the socket write buffers for the same clients are where the 1 Hz timer frames queue.
findings.fix_sketch: Emit one shared `battleSnapshot` to the room (one encode) and send per-user deltas (`free_taps_left`) only when they change (on freeTap) via `user_{id}` room; cache free-tap counts in memory; decouple topTraders from snapshot flush (own 1 s coalescer already exists) and gate dashboards on `trade.executed` only; cap the late-battle gap at ≥200 ms. Files: redis/redis.subscriber.ts, ws/ws.gateway.ts, battle/battle.service.ts.

findings.title: Socket.IO Redis adapter is pure overhead on the single-instance deployment: every room/user emit is msgpack-encoded, PUBLISHed and echoed back for decode
findings.user_symptom: CPU and Redis bandwidth burned per emit; per-user emits (trade:active:stream, balanceEquityAndPnL, tradingDashboard, equityAndPnL, balanceUpdated) multiply it
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/backend/ecosystem.config.js `exec_mode: 'fork', instances: 1`; main.ts:67-75 enables the adapter unless `WS_REDIS_ADAPTER=false`; redis-adapter dist/index.js broadcast(): `if (!onlyLocal) { const msg = this.parser.encode([...]); this.pubClient.publish(channel, msg); } super.broadcast(...)` and onmessage(): `const args = this.parser.decode(msg); ... if (this.uid === uid) return` (decode happens before the self-check). Per-user emits: ws.gateway.ts:519-522 `this.server.to(`user_${userId}`).emit(...)`, used per user per second from trades.service.ts:5064 and redis.subscriber.ts:3520. The adapter's pub client is the same shared command connection used by the trade hot path (redis-io.adapter.ts:29, redis.client.ts:93-102).
findings.mechanism: For each emit: JSON encode (socket.io) + msgpack encode + Redis PUBLISH + subscriber receive + msgpack decode; the PUBLISH traffic shares the ioredis command connection with idempotency/reserve/pot Lua scripts, adding head-of-line latency to trades.
findings.fix_sketch: Set `WS_REDIS_ADAPTER=false` while instances=1, or keep the adapter but use `.local` flag for emits (`this.server.local.to(room).emit`) when a single instance is detected; if clustering later, give the adapter a dedicated pub connection. Files: main.ts, ws/redis-io.adapter.ts, ws/ws.gateway.ts.

findings.title: `chatHistory` with `broadcast_to_all` lets any authenticated user broadcast a 100-message payload to every connected socket, unthrottled
findings.user_symptom: Trivial amplification DoS: one client message → N×(100 rows) fan-out + 3 DB queries per call
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/ws/battle.gateway.ts:571-605: no `wsRateLimit.consume`, no role check; 598-599 `if (data?.broadcast_to_all) { this.server.emit('chatHistory', payload); }`; `getBattleChatMessages` (battle.service.ts:1678-1708) runs findUnique + findMany(include user) + count each time (limit up to 200).
findings.mechanism: Unlimited calls per socket; each triggers a global broadcast of up to 200 messages with user includes.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove `broadcast_to_all` (or restrict to ADMIN role), rate-limit chatHistory (bucket 'chat' or new one), cache the last 100 messages per battle in memory and refresh on chat.message. Files: ws/battle.gateway.ts.

findings.title: Timer relay drop/delay points (engine → Redis → API → sockets)
findings.user_symptom: Countdown jitter, bunched 2→1→0, battleEnd arriving seconds late
findings.evidence: Drops: redis.subscriber.ts:542-548 and 685-687 return without queuing when `!shouldBroadcast()`; ws-broadcaster-leader.service.ts:153-164 flips `isLeader=false` on a single failed/slow renew EVAL before re-acquiring (events during that window are lost; TTL 10 s). Delays: 1245-1280 `flushPendingTimerQueueOnBattleEnd` is awaited at 1466 BEFORE `battleEnd` is emitted (1509) and sleeps `gap` per queued tick (1000 ms for ending), so a 3-deep queue delays battleEnd ≈3 s; 1323-1378 `forwardTimerNow` synchronously kicks `emitActiveTradeStreamUpdatesForBattle` (4 Prisma queries + per-user projections) on every tick; ws.gateway.ts:476-486 `TIMER_YIELD_MS` re-schedules every coalesced per-user emit with a fresh setTimeout per call (thousands of timers per burst). Engine side: battle-engine.service.ts:760 `if (this.heartbeatRunning) return;` then backfills with `backfilled:true` and identical `timestamp: now` (796-811); `void this.events.timerUpdate(...)` (831) has no catch → engine crash if the Redis publish rejects. Emitted only to `battle_${id}` (1323) — sockets still inside the ~50-query subscribe (F7) miss ticks; the `.compress(false)` at ws.gateway.ts:385 is a no-op (engine.io perMessageDeflate off by default).
findings.mechanism: Timer frames share the event loop and the per-socket write queues with F7/F8 work; the pacer adds up to 1 s when the engine is early and the battle.end path serializes behind it.
findings.fix_sketch: Queue (not drop) engine events while not leader and flush on acquire; emit `battleEnd` immediately and let the pacer finish in background; move `emitActiveTradeStreamUpdatesForBattle` off the timer tick to a separate 1 s interval with its own guard; replace per-call setTimeout yield with a single flush timer; add `.catch` on engine `events.timerUpdate`. Files: redis/redis.subscriber.ts, ws/ws.gateway.ts, apps/engine/src/battle/battle-engine.service.ts.

findings.title: activeTradeStream in-flight/pending maps keyed inconsistently → pending stream never delivered and socket reference leaked
findings.user_symptom: After switching battles quickly, trade:active:stream first paint never arrives; memory held per stale socket
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/ws/battle.gateway.ts:27-28 `activeTradeStreamInFlightByUser = new Map<number, number>(); activeTradeStreamPendingAfterFlight = new Map<string, AuthedSocket>();` 316-321 inFlight keyed by `userId`, pending keyed by `${userId}:${battleId}`; 355-362 the finally only looks up `flightKey` of the battle that just finished.

findings.fix_sketch: Key both maps by userId (store latest pending {socket,battleId}) or by `${userId}:${battleId}` consistently; clear on disconnect. Files: ws/battle.gateway.ts.
