findings.title: Queued trades execute in engine-worker where WebsocketGateway has no server: balanceUpdated / notification / equityUpdated emits are silently dropped
findings.user_symptom: After an async trade the user gets trade:buy:result but no balanceUpdated/celebration notification; admins see none of the worker-originated notifications
findings.evidence: engine-worker/engine-worker.module.ts:51 imports TradesModule which imports WsModule (trades.module.ts:24); TradesService injects `WebsocketGateway` directly (trades.service.ts:572) and calls `this.wsGateway.emitToUserCoalesced(userId, 'balanceUpdated', ...)` at 2974, `emitToBattle/emitToUser('notification')` at 3080-3081, `emitToUser('equityUpdated')` at 2984; ws.gateway.ts:40-43 `hasServer()` is false under `createApplicationContext` (engine-worker/main.ts:21) so every emit returns early. BattleService correctly uses `WS_EMIT_PORT` (battle.service.ts:335) but WsModule's LocalWsEmitAdapter (ws.module.ts:46-50) shadows the Redis publisher there too.

findings.user_symptom: Spikes on the chart right after signing in from a phone; phone and web charts differ
findings.evidence: Backend /home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/ws/line-chart.gateway.ts:639-648 `getLastCompletedBattleIds(): where: { status: 'COMPLETED' } ... take: HISTORY_BATTLE_LIMIT` and 820-836 `buildCandleBatchPayload(...) { const includedBattleIds = await this.getLastCompletedBattleIds(); ... for (const bid of includedBattleIds) { const candles = await this.getClosedCandlesForBattle(bid, now); ...` — the active battle id is fetched (823-828) but only echoed as `active_battle_id`, never included. 881-899 `dedupeUnifiedCandlesByTimestamp ... return deduped.slice(-MAX_POINTS)` (MAX_POINTS=200, candle-types.ts:7). Observed live (node socket.io client against 127.0.0.1:18773/line-chart while battle 87 ACTIVE): `candleBatch active_battle_id=87 included=[84,85,86] candles=200 per-battle counts {'86':200}` — zero candles for 87. Redis has the active battle's history (`chart:history:battle_87`, 18 rows) but it is never sent. Client has no backfill path: /home/claude/wb/frontend/src/utils/useWebSocket.js:1591-1611 `requestLineChartBackfill` requires `lineChartBattleCursorRef.current` which the server always sets to `battle_cursor: null` (gateway 871). Client-side candles for the active round come only from live `candleClosed`/`priceUpdate` after connect (useWebSocket.js:636-659, 999-1027). NewChart feeds lightweight-charts plain {time,value} points (NewChart.jsx:189-225 buildSeriesData) with no whitespace points, and lightweight-charts positions bars by index, so a 2-minute hole between battle 86's last candle and the first live tick of 87 is drawn as ONE bar step. Battles are price-continuous (psql: 86 endPrice 1.26384 == 87 startPrice 1.26384), so the whole intra-round move that happened before the client connected appears as a single vertical segment. Same on resume: after backgrounding (iOS kills the socket), reconnect only replays completed battles, so every candle missed while backgrounded is lost and the price move is drawn as a cliff. A web tab open since round start has every candle, hence the two charts differ. hydrateMatchFromResume.js:175-184 restores at most 50 candles and only if the snapshot is < 5 min old (99, 130).
findings.mechanism: Server history excludes the active round and the client never requests/receives it; the chart draws index-spaced bars so a time gap becomes a one-bar vertical jump.
findings.fix_sketch: Backend line-chart.gateway.ts buildCandleBatchPayload: append `getClosedCandlesForBattle(activeBattleId)` (reads chart:history:battle_<id>) plus the in-progress candle from liveCandles, and make the per-battle cap apply after including the active battle (or serve the active battle in its own `subscribe {battleId}` response instead of returning early on scope==='all' at 553-556). Frontend useWebSocket.js: on line-chart connect and on syncNow, emit `subscribe {battleId}` for the active battle and merge; in NewChart.buildSeriesData insert flat/whitespace points for missing seconds (or stop drawing a line across gaps) so a gap can never render as a spike.

findings.title: Foreground/resume triggers two independent forced syncs → 4× subscribeToBattle, 2× line-chart subscribe, up to 4 candleBatch (200 candles each) per resume; server runs the full subscribe pipeline each time
findings.user_symptom: General slowness / delayed info under load (every phone resume fans out DB work and ~1 MB of socket payload); also multiplies F1's replay
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/frontend/src/utils/useWebSocket.js:403-429 registers `document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", syncOnForeground)` + `window.addEventListener("pageshow", ...)` with `const force = type === "visibilitychange" || type === "pageshow"; syncNow({ force, source: type })`. Independently /home/claude/wb/frontend/src/components/ResumeSyncBridge.jsx:57-65 `onForegroundSync = ... ws?.syncNow?.({ force: true, source: 'app-foreground' })` via useRealtimeSync→useAppLifecycle (useAppLifecycle.js:81,85,86 visibilitychange/resume/pageshow). syncNow (364-401): `if (!force && now - lastManualSyncAtRef.current < 500) return;` — force bypasses the dedupe, so both run. Each syncNow: `socketRef.current.emit("subscribeToPrice")` (393) + `emitSubscribeToBattle(..., { includeRange: true })` (395) which emits subscribeToBattle twice (265-270: `socket.emit("subscribeToBattle", basePayload); if (options.includeRange) socket.emit("subscribeToBattle", rangePayload)`) + `forceLineChartSync()` (400 → 357 `lineChartSocket.emit("subscribe", subscribePayload)`). If the socket actually reconnected, onConnect (684-696) adds another subscribeToPrice + 2 subscribeToBattle, and onLineChartConnect (539) another subscribe while the server's handleConnection also emits candleBatch unconditionally (line-chart.gateway.ts:252-263 `this.joinAll(socket); void this.emitCandleBatchOnConnect(socket, null)`) — observed: connect + one subscribe = 2 candleBatch of 200 candles. Server subscribeToBattle (/home/claude/wb/backend/apps/api/src/ws/battle.gateway.ts:117-313) per call: getActiveBattleId, battle.findUnique, emitBootstrapBattleSnapshotToSocket, redis publish battle.join, user.findUnique, getEquityAndPnlForBalanceEvent, getBattleChatMessages(limit 100), getTopTradersForBattle, emitTradingDashboardUpdate (298) AND startTradingDashboardStream (312, same call again), startActiveTradeStream; the `recentDuplicate` guard (192-195, 216) only skips the bootstrap snapshot — chat history, top traders, dashboard×2, trade stream and balance are recomputed for all 4 emits. `subscribeToPrice` has no @SubscribeMessage handler anywhere in apps/api (grep), pure noise.
findings.mechanism: Two lifecycle listeners for the same event, a force flag that defeats the dedupe, includeRange doubling emits, and server handlers that redo all work per emit.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep one foreground path (drop the listeners in useWebSocket.js:403-429 or the ResumeSyncBridge call), make syncNow dedupe even forced calls within ~1 s, send range in the same subscribeToBattle payload instead of a second emit, remove subscribeToPrice, do not emit 'subscribe' in onLineChartConnect when handleConnection already sends candleBatch (or drop the server-side emit-on-connect). Backend battle.gateway.ts: extend the 3 s per-socket dedupe to the whole pipeline and remove the duplicate emitTradingDashboardUpdate (298 vs 312).

findings.title: ResumeSyncBridge persists the whole resume snapshot to sessionStorage on every price tick (throttle written but never wired) — up to ~20 large JSON.stringify writes/s on the phone
findings.user_symptom: Slowness/jank on phones, delayed UI under load
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/frontend/src/components/ResumeSyncBridge.jsx:81-95 selector includes `price: state.price, timer: state.timer` so it fires on every matchStore price/timer write (pricePipeline.js PRICE_THROTTLE_MS=50 → up to 20/s, hotUpdateScheduler cap 30/s). 97-128 define `schedulePersistFromMatchSlice`/`flushMatchResumeSnapshot` with `MATCH_RESUME_PERSIST_THROTTLE_MS = 750` but the subscriber at 130-166 calls `appResumeStore.getState().saveSnapshot({ ... topTraders, topPerformers, activeTrades, finalBattleSnapshot, battleEndData, cooldownDisplay, recentCandles })` directly on every change; `schedulePersistFromMatchSlice` is never referenced. appResumeStore.js:77-129 uses zustand `persist` with `createJSONStorage(() => sessionStorage)` and a partialize that includes topTraders (20 users with avatar URLs), topPerformers, activeTrades (≤20), recentCandles (50), finalBattleSnapshot (≤50 candles + traders) — every set() serialises all of it synchronously. A second subscriber (198-216) also debounces chart saves. The docs claim the opposite (docs/ARCHITECTURE-DATA-FLOW.md:13 'No persistence ... to sessionStorage').
findings.mechanism: Unthrottled zustand-persist write on the hottest store path; JSON.stringify of tens of KB per tick on the main thread.
findings.fix_sketch: Route the subscriber through schedulePersistFromMatchSlice (≥750 ms) and additionally flush on visibilitychange→hidden/pagehide; remove price/timer from the persisted slice (timer is explicitly not rehydrated, hydrateMatchFromResume.js:149) or persist them only on hide.

findings.title: NewChart re-reads and JSON.parses the sessionStorage candle mirror and rebuilds the whole series on every tick flush (≤25×/s); candleClosed re-serialises it every second
findings.user_symptom: Slowness/jank on phones under load
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/frontend/src/components/NewChart.jsx:1371-1375 `lineChartStore.subscribe(selectChartStoreSlice, applyStoreToChart)` fires whenever the last candle's close/volume/ts changes (chartFlushService.js chartPricesSignature) — i.e. every RAF flush of a price tick (useWebSocket.js:1002 forwards at most one tick per 40 ms). applyStoreToChart (1291-1369) then calls `mergePricesWithSessionClosed(candles, activeBattleId)` (1301) → 143-164 → `loadCandleClosedSessionForBattle(bid)` → persistCandleClosedSession.js:6-18 `readState()` = `sessionStorage.getItem(KEY)` + `JSON.parse` of up to 300 candles, then a Map + sort, then `buildSeriesData` (189-225: Map + sort over ≤200 candles) and `saveCachedSeriesForBattle`. On every candleClosed, useWebSocket.js:652 `appendCandleClosedToSession` → persistCandleClosedSession.js:30-61 read+parse+findIndex+sort+`JSON.stringify` write. lineChartStore.appendCandleBatch (120-123) also re-sorts and dedupes the full array per closed candle.
findings.mechanism: O(n log n) rebuild plus synchronous storage parse/serialise on the hot tick path.
findings.fix_sketch: Cache the parsed session candles in module memory (invalidate on battle change) and merge only on mount/battle switch; keep an incremental 'last point' update path for ticks (only call series.update with the new point) and reserve the full rebuild for candleBatch/reset; write the candleClosed mirror from an in-memory array with a debounced stringify.

findings.title: Three perpetual RAF loops plus per-frame forced layout reads keep the phone CPU pinned at 60 fps even when nothing changes
findings.user_symptom: Slowness, battery drain, delayed info on phones
findings.evidence: NewChart.jsx:1036-1155 animate(): once data exists it always ends with `scheduleAnimate()` (1154) and calls `areaSeriesRef.current.update({ time: lastTimeRef.current, value: display })` every frame (1077) with no change check on `display`, redraws the glow canvas with 3 radial gradients + shadowBlur per frame (501-564), and calls `syncRoundEntryLabelY` every frame (1143) which calls `measurePlotOffsetYPx` → two `getBoundingClientRect()` per frame (369-392, 352-359) — contradicting the comment at 334-337 that says offsets are 'never per frame, where it caused layout thrash on mobile' (only the X variant is cached). TradingPanel.jsx:756-781 progress bar: `progressRafIdRef.current = requestAnimationFrame(tick)` unconditionally every frame and `track?.style.setProperty('--sell-percent', ...)` (776) even when `s === target`. realtimeTelemetry.js:51-74 `startDroppedFrameMonitor` (called at useWebSocket.js:455 on every socket hook mount) runs a RAF loop forever; `stopDroppedFrameMonitor` has no callers (grep).
findings.mechanism: Unconditional RAF rescheduling and per-frame chart repaints/layout reads.
findings.fix_sketch: In animate(): stop rescheduling when |display−target| < epsilon and no pending target (restart from tick/candle callbacks), skip series.update when the value is unchanged, run the glow pulse at ≤30 fps, cache the Y offset in the same reseat path as X. TradingPanel: stop the RAF when converged and restart from the sellPercent effect. Telemetry: do not start the frame monitor in production (or stop it on unmount).

findings.title: 'reconnect'/'reconnect_attempt' handlers never fire (socket.io-client v4 emits them on the Manager); reconnect bootstrap and expectFullSnapshot are dead code, and two other dead events exist
findings.user_symptom: Latent: stale delta base after reconnect (no impact today because the backend sends no deltas); wasted emits
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/frontend/src/utils/useWebSocket.js:1353-1354 `socket.on("reconnect_attempt", onReconnectAttempt); socket.on("reconnect", onReconnect);` — socket.io-client 4.8.3: only manager.js:333/365 `emitReserved("reconnect_attempt"...)`/`emitReserved("reconnect", attempt)`; socket.js emits no such reserved events (socket.js:592 only `connect`). So onReconnect (1254-1270: `expectFullSnapshotRef.current = true; ... handleReconnectSuccess(...)`) never runs; reconnect resubscription only works because onConnect (673) also fires. Backend has no delta emitters (grep `battleSnapshotDelta|battleSnapshot_delta|price_delta|priceDelta` in apps/api/src → none), so the delta path (805-838) is unreachable; likewise `socket.on("marketSnapshot", ...)` (1358) has no emitter (grep 'marketSnapshot' in backend → none) and `subscribeToPrice` (324, 393, 684, 1280) has no @SubscribeMessage handler.
findings.mechanism: Wrong event target for manager-level events; dead contracts left in place.
findings.fix_sketch: Use `socket.io.on('reconnect', ...)` / `socket.io.on('reconnect_attempt', ...)` (and off them on cleanup); delete the marketSnapshot listener, subscribeToPrice emits and the delta branches, or implement them server-side.

findings.title: Live stream and history have different bar density (server stores flat gap candles but never emits them), and candleBatch's included_battle_ids is not what is sent
findings.user_symptom: Phone and web charts differ (x-compression), different 'shape' of the same round
findings.evidence: line-chart.gateway.ts:448-467 `pushHistoryAndEmitCandleClosed` fills every missing second with `emitFlatCandleForGap` (413-446) which only writes historyByKey/Redis — no publishChartEvent — while only real tick buckets are emitted (523-526). Redis `chart:history:battle_87` shows 1-second rows with `volume:0,count:0`. The client builds bars only from priceUpdate ticks/candleClosed (useWebSocket.js:999-1027, 636-659), so a client connected live has bars only for seconds with trades, whereas a client that (re)connects receives flat-filled history at 1 bar/s. In addition 881-899 dedupes across all included battles and `slice(-MAX_POINTS)` (200) — observed payload claimed `included=[84,85,86]` but contained only 200 candles of battle 86.
findings.mechanism: Asymmetric gap filling between stored history and the live feed; global 200-candle cap applied after the per-battle merge.
findings.fix_sketch: Either emit the flat gap candles to clients (candleClosed with count 0) or synthesise 1-second flat bars on the client in buildSeriesData; make `included_battle_ids` reflect the candles actually sent and apply the cap per battle.

findings.title: Service worker/PWA build config: hashed immutable assets use NetworkFirst (network round-trip on every load), most route chunks are not precached, and console stripping is silently ignored (invalid Vite key)
findings.user_symptom: Slower app start on mobile networks; noisy console in prod. NOT a cause of stale chart data: API origin (VITE_APP_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18773 vs app on 18771) matches no runtimeCaching rule
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/frontend/vite.config.js:26-31 `globPatterns: ['**/*.{ico,woff2}', 'assets/AppShell-*.js', 'assets/react-*.js', 'assets/react-dom-*.js']` (Matches/NewChart/lightweight-charts/socket chunks not precached); 51-75 `handler: 'NetworkFirst'` for `path.startsWith('/assets/')` with no `networkTimeoutSeconds`, although dist/_headers marks /assets/* `immutable`; 44-50 NetworkOnly for navigations; both rules require `url.origin === self.location.origin` (46, 54) so API/socket URLs are never cached (confirmed safe). 149-152 `esbuildOptions: { drop: ['debugger'], pure: ['console.log', ...] }` under `build` is not a Vite option (Vite uses top-level `esbuild`); dist/assets/App-COA40tHj.js still contains 'balanceEquityAndPnL ignored' (console.warn string) — 38 console.* calls remain in src.
findings.mechanism: Misconfigured workbox strategy for immutable files and a mis-nested esbuild option.
findings.fix_sketch: Use CacheFirst (or StaleWhileRevalidate) for /assets/*, add the arena chunks to globPatterns, move `pure`/`drop` to top-level `esbuild: {...}`.

findings.title: Resume snapshot (sessionStorage) is replayed into live stores on boot and is never cleared on logout — stale price/trades/balance from the previous session (or previous user in the same tab) paint before socket data
findings.user_symptom: Stale/odd values right after sign-in on a phone (price badge, active trades, balance/equity) until the socket overwrites them
findings.evidence: /home/claude/wb/frontend/src/stores/appResumeStore.js:124-127 `onRehydrateStorage: () => (state) => hydrateMatchStoreFromResume(state)`; hydrateMatchFromResume.js:130 accepts anything < 5 min old and 150-164 applies `restorePriceFromSnapshot(snapshot.price)`, `portfolioStore.setBalanceEquityDisplay(snapshot.balanceEquityDisplay)`, `setTopTradersUpdate`, `tradeFeedStore.setActiveTradesBatch(trades)`, plus candles. `clearSnapshot` (appResumeStore.js:84) has no callers (grep); authStore.logout (authStore.js:120-170) and clearStorageOnLoginRedirect.js only touch localStorage. ProtectedRoute.jsx:372-383 renders children before auth init purely because a resume snapshot exists. matchStore.setPrice from the snapshot feeds PriceBadge.jsx:18 immediately.
findings.mechanism: Persisted per-tab UI state is treated as truth on boot without user/session binding or a clear on logout.
findings.fix_sketch: Call appResumeStore.clearSnapshot() (and clear the candleClosed/sessionBattleId keys) in logout/clearStorageOnRedirectToLogin; store the user id in the snapshot and ignore it on mismatch; do not hydrate price/activeTrades/balanceEquityDisplay (let the socket bootstrap fill them), keep only route/battleId/candles.

findings.title: NewChart and PriceBadge re-render on every snapshot/timer/tick even though they only need the chart engine refs
findings.user_symptom: Extra React work per second on phones
findings.evidence: NewChart.jsx:598-616 `matchStore(useShallow((s) => ({ ..., lastLiveSnapshot: s.lastLiveSnapshot, ..., serverTimer: s.timer })))` → re-render on every 500 ms snapshot push and every timerUpdate; effects at 1501-1504 and 1506-1523 depend on `countdownSecondsLeft`/`serverTimer?.timestamp` so `subscribeVisibleTimeRangeChange`/`unsubscribe` + `reseatExpiryMap` (two getBoundingClientRect) re-run every second; 1533-1539 `timerDisplay` rendered in JSX. PriceBadge.jsx:20-23 selects `prices[prices.length - 1]` (a new object per flush) so it re-renders per tick flush.
findings.mechanism: Broad selectors on hot stores inside components that mostly use refs.
findings.fix_sketch: Select only the scalar fields needed (end_time, is_finalize, time_remaining), move the countdown text into a tiny child component, and make PriceBadge select the last close number rather than the object.
